runtime: Bash builtins and POSIX utilities (no types, no source)
conventions: Symbols are command words, matched by spelling when the word does not resolve to a function. Positions count the words after the command word. {"code": i}: word i is a string parsed as Bash commands (tree-sitter-bash). {"command": i}: the first word at or after i that is not an option or an assignment starts a command. {"kw": "-F"}: the word following option -F.

entries.describe: trap 'commands' SIGNAL runs the commands when the signal (EXIT, ERR, INT, DEBUG, RETURN ...) arrives
entries.why: Bash builtin: the handler is a string parsed as code at signal time

entries.describe: eval 'commands' runs its (concatenated) arguments as commands now
entries.why: Bash builtin: the argument is a string parsed as code

entries.describe: time cmd runs cmd (a function too) and reports its duration
complete -F func name registers func as the completion function of name
entries.why: Bash builtin: the function is named by a word

entries.describe: mapfile -C func calls func every -c lines while reading
entries.why: Bash builtin: the function is named by a word

entries.describe: command/builtin/exec name run a builtin or program named name, never a shell function of that name
entries.why: Bash builtin: function lookup is skipped by definition

entries.describe: timeout DURATION cmd runs cmd as a separate program; a shell function name there is not called
entries.why: external program: it execs a file, shell functions are not visible to it

entries.describe: these run their command as a separate program; a shell function name there is not called (only scripts and programs)
entries.why: external programs: they exec a file, shell functions are not visible to them

io_send.describe: a simple command whose word is not a function, alias or builtin runs the program found on PATH (or by path)
